inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report & Form 20-F, Group cash flow statement 'Equity-settled share-based payments cost' $72m (IHG.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:13631 reconciliation) plus $10m cash tax withheld on net-settled awards (EquityAwardTaxes kpi). No combined figure published, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 June 2026: 157m shares in issue at 31 Dec 2025 (FY2025 AR note 28) less 2.7m repurchased and cancelled in H1 2026 (H1 2026 note 7) = 154.3m in issue; less ~5.6m treasury/non-dividend shares (basic weighted average 150.0m for H1 implies ~148.7m basic at period end) plus 1.1m dilutive potential shares (H1 2026 note 8) = 149.8m diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. The remaining ~$550m of the 2026 $950m buyback is value-neutral in this model (cash out = shares in).
inputs.fx_note: IHG changed the currency of its LSE share price from British pounds to US dollars (FY2025 Annual Report, Board decisions: 'The Board approved the change of the Company's share price currency from British Pounds to US Dollars'). Yahoo Finance reports IHG.L meta currency USD on exchange LSE with a continuous USD series (52-week 117.9-175.7). Parity check: NYSE ADR IHG (1 ADS = 1 ordinary share) printed within 1.0% of the LSE line at the same date, the gap being the three-hour close-time difference. Financials are presented in millions of US dollars, so no FX bridge is needed; fx_rate = 1.0. GBPUSD 1.3233 (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-09) is recorded only for readers converting to sterling.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company-defined net debt at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 note 10): cash $825m; loans and other borrowings $1,046m current + $3,101m non-current; lease liabilities $32m current + $362m non-current; principal receivable on maturity of currency swaps +$53m. total_debt here is borrowings plus leases net of the $53m swap principal receivable (4,541 - 53 = 4,488) so that total_debt - cash = 3,663 ties to the company figure. Net debt:adjusted EBITDA 2.63x against a 2.5-3.0x target range (investment grade).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built WACC. Cost of equity ~9.5% (10y UST ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.05 for a fee-based lodging franchisor); after-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (bonds 3-5% coupons, 27% tax); debt ~13% of enterprise value at the current price (net debt $3.7bn vs ~$24bn market cap) gives ~8.7%, rounded to 8.75%. One WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality and the China/US RevPAR risks are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt: IFRS 16 lease liabilities ($394m at 30 June 2026) sit inside net debt and lease principal ($30m FY2025) is NOT deducted from the flows; adjusted EBITDA is the post-IFRS-16 figure. Owned/leased hotel renewal capex is inside the capex line. Lease interest ($30m) is a financing cost covered by WACC.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is immaterial ($5m stock, $1m of profit in FY2025): flows taken as consolidated, no NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US', owner-fcf.md plus the adaptations file for currency, leases and NCI). IHG is an asset-light franchisor/manager: 1.03m rooms, ~99% franchised or managed, fee revenue $1,897m (FY2025) at a 65.9% fee margin (H1 2026). Revenue base is the statutory total revenue of $5,189m, which INCLUDES System Fund and reimbursement revenue ($2,721m, pass-through at ~zero margin) so that it ties to the Metrics CSV history; margins are therefore expressed on total revenue (adjusted EBITDA = adjusted operating profit $1,265m + D&A $146m = $1,411m, 27.2% of total revenue; equivalently ~57% of revenue from reportable segments). Capex line includes key money contract acquisition costs ($179m gross FY2025, which IHG books inside operating cash flow) plus maintenance/IT capex, i.e. net capital expenditure $185m per the company's own KPM, ~3.3-3.6% of total revenue - this is the real cost of the pipeline, not the $77m statutory PP&E+intangibles line. Working capital capture 10% of the revenue change reflects the growing deferred loyalty/application-fee liability inside OCF. Interest income $49m is NOT stripped: IHG is a net borrower (net debt 2.6x EBITDA), so there is no cash pile to double-count. Shareholders' equity is NEGATIVE (-$2,978m at 30 June 2026) as a disclosed consequence of $3.7bn of buybacks since 2022 on an asset-light balance sheet; it is a capital-allocation choice, not distress - book-value multiples, equity CAGR and P/B sanity checks are meaningless here. Buyback_cash $897m is the FY2025 programme (financing outflow); the 2026 programme is $950m, 42% complete at 30 June. last_fcf is owner FCF on the company's levered reported basis (OCF $898m - PP&E $28m - intangibles $49m = $821m, less SBC incl. equity-award taxes $82m); the forward build is unlevered from EBITDA, so the two are not directly comparable - the unlevered FY2025 owner FCF implied by the component build is ~$865m, versus ~$853m from the reported figure after adding back after-tax net interest. FY2026 is three-quarters elapsed: year 1 of the build is FY2026 discounted a full period, which is conservative by a few percent. H1 2026 actuals: revenue +5.6%, fee revenue +7%, adjusted operating profit +10% to $665m, adjusted EPS +13%, net debt +$330m on $564m of shareholder returns. Q3 trading update due 22 October 2026.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Forward: management's medium-term algorithm (high-single-digit fee revenue growth, 100-150bps annual fee-margin expansion) applied to total revenue including the lower-growth System Fund/reimbursement pass-through; tempered to 5.5-6% near term and decelerating. Equity CAGR is unusable because book value is negative.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' equity is negative throughout the history (-$1,481m FY2021 to -$2,978m H1 FY2026) because cumulative buybacks exceed retained earnings on an asset-light balance sheet; equity CAGR cannot be computed and is not a valid growth proxy here. The FY2021-FY2025 CAGRs are inflated by the COVID recovery base (FY2021 revenue $2,907m vs $4,627m in FY2019-equivalent); the FY2022-FY2025 3-year figures are the cleaner read. Owner-FCF CAGR (13.9% 3yr) sits just below reported FCF CAGR (14.5%) because SBC plus equity-award taxes rose from $47m to $82m over the period - modest, and SBC is only 1.6% of revenue.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes; interest income not stripped, net borrower): FY2021 543, FY2022 500, FY2023 747, FY2024 552, FY2025 739 ($m). FY2024 was depressed by working-capital timing and a $309m cash tax year; FY2023 was flattered by a working-capital inflow. Only five annual periods are in the CSV, so 5-year CAGRs are null and 4-year (FY2021-FY2025) figures are given instead.

base.narrative: Management algorithm delivered at the lower-middle of its range: net system growth ~4% plus RevPAR +1-2% gives fee revenue +6-7%; total revenue (incl. System Fund pass-through) +5.5-6% then decelerating to 3%. Fee margin expands ~100bps/yr, which on total revenue is ~+0.5pp/yr of adjusted EBITDA margin, from 27.2% (FY2025) to ~31% by year 10. Key money and maintenance capex 3.3% of total revenue easing to 3.0% as the pipeline matures. Cash tax at the guided 26-27% adjusted rate.

bull.narrative: Algorithm delivered at the top of its range: RevPAR re-accelerates to +3-4% as US supply growth stays at 0.4-1% and Greater China recovers; signings of 100k+ rooms a year convert and net system growth reaches 5%+; fee margin expands 150bps/yr with co-brand card, loyalty-point and residences fees scaling. Higher key money spend (3.5% of revenue) funds the faster pipeline conversion.

bear.narrative: A 2027-28 US lodging downturn: RevPAR falls mid-single digits for two years (as in 2001-02 and 2008-09, when IHG's fee revenue fell ~10-15%), offset only partly by system growth; owners defer renovations and conversions, signings slow, and Greater China stays weak. Operating leverage runs in reverse - fee margin gives back ~2pp before stabilising - and the company keeps growing at trend thereafter but from a lower base, with no further margin expansion. Terminal multiple capped at 15x to reflect the cyclicality of the earnings stream.

scenario_narratives.base: IHG keeps compounding as an asset-light fee business. Net system size grows ~4% a year (1.03m rooms, 340k-room pipeline, 100k+ rooms signed in each of 2024 and 2025) and global RevPAR adds +1-2% in a mid-cycle environment, giving fee revenue growth of 6-7% - the lower-middle of management's 'high-single-digit' algorithm. Fee margin rises ~100bps a year from 65.9% through operating leverage as the fee cost base is held to 1-3% growth, which is ~0.5pp a year on the total-revenue EBITDA margin used here. Key money of ~$180m a year keeps funding conversions. Net debt stays in the 2.5-3.0x target range with ~$950m a year of buybacks, which are value-neutral in this model (SBC expensed, count flat). Near term, the H1 2026 run-rate (revenue +5.6%, fee revenue +7%, adjusted operating profit +10%) carries into year 1.
scenario_narratives.bull: The structural tailwinds management cites compound together: hotel room nights grow at the 3.6% decade CAGR Oxford Economics forecasts while US net supply growth sits below 1%, lifting RevPAR to +3-4%; Greater China returns to growth; conversions (Garner, Ruby, voco) accelerate net system growth to 5%+; the 2024-25 step-ups in co-brand card and loyalty-point fees become ongoing growth streams; and fee margin expands at the top of the 100-150bps range. Adjusted EPS compounds at the upper end of the 12-15% target. The DCF then approaches today's premium multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Lodging is cyclical and IHG's fee stream is geared to it: in the 2008-09 downturn RevPAR fell ~10% and fee revenue dropped double digits. A 2027-28 US-led recession (the Americas is ~60% of fee operating profit), a prolonged Greater China slump, or a geopolitical travel shock cuts RevPAR for two years while owners stall conversions and signings; margin gives back ~2pp through negative operating leverage. Leverage at 2.6x EBITDA remains serviceable but the buyback pace halves. Growth resumes at trend from a lower base, and the market re-rates IHG from ~25x to a mid-cycle 15x FCF. Not a solvency case: the business stays cash generative throughout.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the house 15% to 20% because lodging demand is genuinely cyclical and IHG's fee stream has fallen double digits in each of the last three recessions, with the Americas providing ~60% of fee profit; the bear case is a downturn plus re-rating, not solvency, so it is not pushed higher. Bull trimmed from 35% to 30% because the bull case needs three independent things - RevPAR re-acceleration, a China recovery and top-of-range margin expansion - to coincide. Base 50%: the company has met every component of its growth algorithm in each of the last four years.

valuation_philosophy.summary: IHG is a high-quality, asset-light compounder - 1.03m rooms almost entirely franchised or managed, a 66% fee margin, ~100% conversion of adjusted earnings into free cash flow, and a disciplined return of all surplus cash through dividends and buybacks funded within a 2.5-3.0x leverage band. The house model values that stream on a strict owner-FCF basis (SBC and equity-award taxes expensed, key money treated as the growth capex it is, leases held as debt, one 8.75% USD WACC, terminal value the lower of Gordon at 3% and a 20x cap). The market pays a premium multiple (~25x adjusted earnings, ~2.6x net debt/EBITDA) for the predictability of the fee algorithm; the DCF asks what that algorithm is worth at a normal discount rate rather than whether the multiple will persist. Negative book equity is a disclosed capital-allocation outcome, not a risk signal.
key_risks_to_valuation: Lodging-cycle risk: RevPAR is procyclical and the Americas (~60% of fee operating profit) drive it; the last three recessions each cut IHG fee revenue by double digits.
Greater China (~8% of fee revenue, ~11% of system) has had weak RevPAR for two years; a prolonged slump drags system growth and signings.
Fee-margin expansion depends on holding the fee cost base to 1-3% growth; technology, loyalty and brand-launch spend could outrun that.
Key money intensity: securing conversions and new-build signings costs ~$180m a year and is rising; if it keeps growing faster than fees the asset-light economics erode.

Leverage at 2.6x net debt/EBITDA with $1.0bn of borrowings current at 30 June 2026 (2027 bond maturities) - refinancing is routine for an investment-grade issuer but raises the interest bill ($230-240m guided for 2026).
Terminal value is ~60% of enterprise value; each 1pp on WACC moves the base value by roughly 15%.
Share-price currency changed from GBP to USD in 2025-26: compare IHG.L only against USD figures; sterling-based investors carry GBPUSD exposure.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_note: Multiples sanity check: P/E, EV/EBITDA and P/S all pass, each below its FY2021-FY2025 average. The only trip is the P/B rule, which is void on negative book equity (see warnings[0]); the valuation was deliberately NOT adjusted for it. Negative equity here is the arithmetic of a franchisor that returns more than it earns through buybacks, not a solvency signal: net debt/adjusted EBITDA is 2.63x inside the 2.5-3.0x investment-grade target.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for IHG.L (LSE, quoted in USD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 117.9-175.7; parity-checked against the NYSE ADR IHG (1:1).
data_sources.financials: IHG.L_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2021-FY2025 annual, H1 FY2023-H1 FY2026 half-years, USD millions) derived from the Annual Report and Form 20-F 2025 (net debt note 22, equity note 28, EPS note, cash flow statement) and the 2026 Half Year Results (notes 7, 8, 10; growth-algorithm and outlook sections).

warnings.message: scripts/sanity_check.py trips on 'Implied P/B -6.43x exceeds 1.5x the 10yr maximum -7.20x'. IHG's shareholders' equity is negative (-$2,978m at 30 June 2026) because $3.7bn of buybacks since 2022 exceed retained earnings on an asset-light balance sheet - a disclosed capital-allocation choice, not distress. A P/B comparison between two negative numbers is meaningless and the rule is arithmetically inverted: any valuation fix that LOWERS the IV moves implied P/B toward zero and trips harder, so none of the documented fix levers (mid-cycle FCF, WACC premium, growth cap, exit-multiple cap) can clear it, and none was applied. The three meaningful rules pass with the implied multiples BELOW their historical averages: P/E 25.7x (hist 23.4-52.9x, avg 36.5x), EV/EBITDA 16.3x (15.6-21.5x, avg 19.0x), P/S 3.4x (3.0-4.4x, avg 3.8x). The P/B rule needs a negative-book-value guard in the checker (a scripts/ change, outside this agent's scope).
